title: Psalm 150: Let Everything That Has Breath Praise the LORD
summary: The last psalm is a single sustained call to praise. It says where to praise God (in his sanctuary and his heavens), why (for his mighty acts and surpassing greatness), how (with horn, harp, lyre, tambourine, dancing, strings, flute, and cymbals), and who should do it: everything that has breath.

from.where: The Study Bible's introduction to the Psalms
from.text: on to a final crescendo in which every psalm from 146 to 150 begins and ends with Hallelujah, praise the LORD.

line: The last psalm: praise God in his sanctuary and his heavens, for his mighty acts, with every instrument, and let everything that has breath praise the LORD.
guide: You do not need to feel like praising to begin; many of the psalms before this one began in the dark. Add your breath to the sound. Jews and Christians still pray and sing the Psalms every day, and the last word of the book can be yours too.

stanzas.title: Where: in his sanctuary and in his heavens
Why: his mighty acts and surpassing greatness
How: with every instrument and with dancing

verses.t: Hallelujah! Praise God in His sanctuary. Praise Him in His mighty heavens.
Praise Him for His mighty acts; praise Him for His excellent greatness.
Praise Him with the sound of the horn; praise Him with the harp and lyre.
Praise Him with tambourine and dancing; praise Him with strings and flute.
Praise Him with clashing cymbals; praise Him with resounding cymbals.
Let everything that has breath praise the LORD! Hallelujah!
